content_blocks.steps_heading: Your Path to PMP Certification in Kansas City

steps_items.heading: Confirm Your Eligibility
steps_items.text: PMI requires either a bachelor's degree plus three years of project-leadership experience, or a high school diploma plus five years of equivalent experience. Review PMI's specific education and hours-worked criteria before applying. Granite PM Academy staff can clarify whether your background meets the credential's requirements.

steps_items.heading: Complete 35 Contact Hours of Training
steps_items.text: Enroll in Granite PM Academy's live-virtual, instructor-led PMP Certification Training course. This formal education covers all domains of the PMP exam and is delivered entirely online, allowing Kansas City professionals to learn on a flexible schedule without commuting to a classroom.

steps_items.heading: Submit Your PMI Application
steps_items.text: After completing the 35-hour course, submit your PMI application with proof of your education and project experience. Pay PMI's exam fee to officially register for the PMP exam. Granite PM Academy will guide you through the submission process and eligibility documentation.

steps_items.heading: Prepare and Take the Exam
steps_items.text: Use Granite PM Academy's exam-preparation resources, practice tests, and instructor feedback to strengthen your readiness. Schedule your exam through PMI's testing partner. Pass the computer-based PMP exam to earn your credential—a recognized standard for project managers across Kansas City's engineering, construction, healthcare, and technology sectors.

steps_items.heading: Maintain Your PMP Credential
steps_items.text: PMP certification is valid for three years. During this cycle, earn professional development units (PDUs) through continuing education, volunteer work, or published contributions to maintain your credential. Plan your PDU strategy early to ensure continuous compliance with PMI's renewal requirements.

fq_items.question: What are the PMP eligibility requirements?
fq_items.answer: PMI sets four eligibility paths based on education: a secondary diploma (high school or equivalent) requires 60 months of project leadership experience; an associate's degree requires 48 months; a bachelor's degree requires 36 months; and a bachelor's or postgraduate degree from a PMI Global Accreditation Center (GAC)-accredited program requires just 24 months. Every path also requires 35 hours of project management education — our course satisfies this requirement in full.

fq_items.question: How long does it take to get PMP certified in {city}?
fq_items.answer: After completing training, PMI typically approves applications within 5–10 business days. Once approved, you have one year to sit for the exam. Most students study 4–8 weeks after the course before scheduling their exam.

fq_items.question: What is your pass guarantee?
fq_items.answer: If you complete our course and do not pass the PMP exam within 90 days, we provide additional coaching sessions at no additional cost until you pass.
